meeting_header:
Date: 2025-06-12
Time: 15:00 - 15:47 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Reddy (Redwood SE), Marco Silva (StratoChip Head of Partnerships), Lina Zhou (StratoChip Technical Partnerships), Owen Park (StratoChip Solutions Architect)
summary: Introductory partner discovery call between Redwood and StratoChip to explore reseller/technology partnership. Discussed go-to-market motions, technical integration points (dedicated pools, private deployment/VPC, hardware compatibility), and a short PoC to validate performance. Security, commercial model, and next steps captured.
topics: Partnership models: reseller vs referral vs technology integration
Technical compatibility: GPU SKUs, drivers, network (VPC/peering), KMS
PoC scope: benchmark metrics (latency, throughput, cost), test datasets
Security/compliance: SOC2, audit logs, data residency
Operational integration: provisioning, billing, support handoff
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, AE. I have Priya our SE with me. How are you all?
[00:08] Marco Silva: Good, thanks. Marco here. Excited to learn more — we saw the request from our partnerships team.
[00:15] Priya Reddy: Hi Marco, Lina, Owen — quick agenda: intro, high-level go-to-market, then a technical section to see where the fit is, and propose next steps. Sound OK?
[00:25] Lina Zhou: Yep, works for us.
[00:30] Owen Park: Also want to make sure we cover hardware compat, like which GPU SKUs Redwood supports and driver requirements.
[00:36] Alex Kim: Totally. At a high level Redwood is an inference platform that runs hosted, dedicated, and private deploys. For partners like StratoChip we typically explore either reselling Dedicated capacity or integrating our Private deployment into your hardware stack.
[00:48] Marco Silva: Our GTM is focused on enterprise telco and finance accounts — low-latency inference is a big ask. We're curious if Redwood can cert performance on our GPU appliances.
[00:59] Priya Reddy: Yes — we do performance profiles per model and hardware. We also provide quantization recommendations and kernel selection in the runtime. For a PoC we'd run benchmarks with your SKUs, measure p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:20] Owen Park: Quick Q — how do you handle private deployments networking? VPC peering, on-prem air-gapped?
[01:28] Priya Reddy: Both. For VPC we do a private control plane option; for air-gapped we provide an on-prem package. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and expose audit logs. There are some differences in upgrade paths, but we have docs.
[01:42] Lina Zhou: Good. Security is a gate for our customers — SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, and log retention are big.
[01:50] Alex Kim: We can share our SOC2 summary and SSO/SAML integration guide. Most enterprise buyers also want a runbook for incident response — we can include that.
[02:02] Marco Silva: On the commercial side, do you do reseller margins or channel referral fees?
[02:08] Alex Kim: We are flexible. For partners who want to resell Dedicated capacity we do committed capacity contracts and can accommodate channel pricing. For referral we track deals in CRM and provide a referral fee. We should map to accounts you target.
[02:22] Marco Silva: OK. For the technical part — Priya, can you outline what you'd need from StratoChip to stand up a PoC?
[02:29] Priya Reddy: Sure. Ideally we need: access to a test node or image with the GPU SKU & driver stack, SSH/remote access to run workloads or a VM image, network topology (VPC/subnet), and a sample workload representing customer sequences — typical lengths and concurrency. We'll also need credential access to KMS if testing encryption in transit.
[02:50] Owen Park: We can provide a VM image and a small cluster; drivers are 525.xx (NVIDIA) and one of our newer Ampere cards.
[02:58] Priya Reddy: Great — latest Ampere is on our supported list but we do microbenchmarks because perf changes with sequence length and quantization bitwidth.
[03:09] Alex Kim: One thing to watch is kernel compatibility — some vendor-specific drivers tweak CUDA behaviours which affects kernel selection. We usually run a quick compile and sample inference to validate.
[03:20] Lina Zhou: About billing integration — can you expose usage APIs we can call to reconcile reseller billing?
[03:26] Alex Kim: Yes, Redwood exposes per-token and per-embedding metering via APIs and the Console. For Dedicated we can also provide token-level breakdowns and route-based cost reporting.
[03:38] Marco Silva: On reliability, do you offer fallbacks if a node goes down? Like routing to hosted or other capacity?
[03:44] Priya Reddy: Absolutely. Smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or other regions. For Dedicated pools we can configure fallback to hosted with controls to avoid data leakage — e.g., only for public models, or never for private deployments.
[03:58] Owen Park: That distinction is important. Many of our customers require data never leave on-prem.
[04:04] Alex Kim: Understood — for those cases we'd recommend the Private/on-prem package and an SLA-backed Dedicated offering for those comfortable with hosted fallback.
[04:15] Marco Silva: What about integration effort — how long to go from contract to GA for a partner offering?
[04:21] Alex Kim: Typically 4-8 weeks for an MVP/reseller flow — depends on integration touchpoints (billing, SSO, packaging). A deeper on-prem certified offering can be 8-16 weeks with driver validation and packaging.
[04:34] Priya Reddy: For the PoC we usually do a 2-week technical sprint: week 1 deploy + baseline benchmarks; week 2 optimize batching, KV cache, and quantization, then produce a report.
[04:47] Marco Silva: Sounds reasonable. Can you call out what metrics you'll report?
[04:52] Priya Reddy: Sure: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, GPU utilization, memory footprint, cost per 1M tokens extrapolated, and regression tests on output quality for quantized variants.
[05:07] Owen Park: On models — do you support switching model variants for cost vs quality tradeoffs? Like smaller quantized vs full fp16?
[05:14] Priya Reddy: Yes. We support model routing and can fallback to quantized variants. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles based on workload. We monitor quality with evals attached to prompts so we can alert on regressions.
[05:30] Lina Zhou: A little noisy here — sorry if I missed — do you support in-line function/tool calling? Some of our customers use LLMs to call downstream services.
[05:38] Alex Kim: Yes, we support streaming responses and function/tool calling patterns.
[05:42] Marco Silva: Any limitations around model size per node? If we pack multiple smaller models on a single appliance how does Redwood manage memory?
[05:50] Priya Reddy: Runtime manages KV cache per session and can do model placement across GPUs; packing depends on VRAM and sequence lengths. For multi-tenant packing we recommend isolation on Dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[06:05] Owen Park: For the PoC we'd like to test both single-model latency and multi-tenant packing to see efficacy.
[06:11] Priya Reddy: Perfect — that's in scope. We'll include packing scenarios in the benchmark plan.
[06:15] Alex Kim: Let's talk success criteria — Marco, what would make this partnership successful in 90 days?
[06:20] Marco Silva: A clear PoC that proves low-latency on your stack on our hardware, a reseller commercial term drafted, and at least one joint customer pilot sign-up.
[06:31] Alex Kim: Good. We'll align on that. Any blockers on your side?
[06:36] Lina Zhou: Need to review SOC2 and make sure we can sign an NDA for more detailed security info.
[06:42] Alex Kim: We can send SOC2 summary and NDA template afterward.
[06:46] Marco Silva: How do you handle support handoff? If we resell, will Redwood white-label or will customers call Redwood?
[06:53] Alex Kim: We support flexible models — partner-led first-line support with Redwood escalation, or direct Redwood support depending on the contract. We can include SLAs and support playbooks.
[07:05] Owen Park: Tech detail — do you require specific kernel modules or is user-space only?
[07:10] Priya Reddy: Mostly user-space runtime and standard drivers, but some telemetry and monitoring agents may need kernel-level access for accurate GPU telemetry. We'll document the exact requirements for the PoC image.
[07:23] Marco Silva: Competitors — our CTO mentioned we should benchmark you against NVIDIA's inference stack and Paperspace. Are you OK with that?
[07:31] Alex Kim: Yeah, benchmarking against others is normal. We welcome it; having third-party comparisons helps the conversation.
[07:36] Priya Reddy: For fairness we ask for the same workload and environment for each baseline.
[07:40] Marco Silva: Great. Any questions from our side we haven't covered?
[07:45] Lina Zhou: What does your partner co-marketing look like? Joint case studies? Demos?
[07:50] Alex Kim: We do co-marketing for strategic partners — joint webinars, co-branded collateral, and case studies once we have a pilot. We also have partner portal access for joint leads.
[07:59] Marco Silva: OK. I think next steps are clear. Can you summarize the PoC timeline?
[08:05] Priya Reddy: Two-week PoC: week 1 deploy & baseline, week 2 optimize & report. We'll deliver a benchmark spreadsheet and a recommendations doc.
[08:14] Owen Park: For the baseline we'll send workload traces and a VM image by next Tuesday.
[08:19] Alex Kim: Great. We'll send SOC2 and partner deck by Monday and a proposed PoC scope by Wednesday.
[08:26] Marco Silva: Super. Anything else?
[08:29] Alex Kim: One more thing on integrations — billing APIs and metering will be exposed; we'll include the API keys and sample scripts in the PoC repo.
[08:38] Lina Zhou: Perfect. Thanks.
[08:40] [CROSSTALK] Everyone: thanks, bye.
[08:44] Alex Kim: Recap of next steps: Alex send SOC2 & partner deck; Priya send PoC scope & measurement plan; Owen send VM image + workload traces; Marco confirm commercial model. We'll reconvene for a technical deep dive mid-next-week.
[08:58] Marco Silva: Sounds good. Appreciate the time.
[09:02] Priya Reddy: Thanks all.
[09:05] [END]
